title: Compatibility shim for OpenAI-style tool calling and legacy functions
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Background: We support two tool/function calling styles in the platform today: (1) OpenAI-style tool calling where the model emits a tool name and JSON args for a declared schema, and (2) legacy 'functions' used by older SDKs where invocation shapes and naming differ (snake_case vs camelCase, different top-level keys, and a subset of structured-output signal conventions). Several customers have started migrating to OpenAI-style tool manifests but still have internal workflows (and older client libraries) that emit legacy function calls. We need a compatibility shim in the API/SDK layer that: - accepts both tool formats at the same endpoint with minimal friction for customers - preserves streaming semantics (token delta events and function call in-stream) - maps names and argument shapes predictably (configurable mapping) - provides transparent telemetry and migration hints

Goal: Implement an API compatibility layer and a reference SDK shim that normalizes legacy function calls into the OpenAI-style tool format before runtime routing, and normalizes runtime responses back to the legacy format when needed. The shim must be opt-in per-API-key and configurable at the route level for Dedicated/Private customers.

Design constraints and decisions: - Non-breaking: Default behavior stays the same for existing hosted API users. Shim is enabled via a per-route flag (compat_tool_shim=true) or per-key migration toggle. - Name mapping: Provide three mapping strategies: identity, canonicalize (snake_case <-> camelCase conversion), and explicit map (user-supplied mapping table). These are chosen because many compatibility issues are simple case differences; explicit map covers complex renames. - Schema compatibility: If a legacy function lacks a formal JSON schema, the shim will infer a loose schema from sample calls (up to first N invocations) and emit a best-effort JSON schema to the runtime with a 'compatibility: inferred' tag. Users are warned in telemetry and Console. - Streaming: For streaming responses, the shim must deliver the same sequence of events to the client. When the model decides to call a tool during a stream, we emit a function_call event consistent with the client's mode: OpenAI-style consumers get the tool call object; legacy consumers get a function invocation blob under the legacy top-level key. We must avoid duplicating payloads. - Error mapping: Runtime errors from tools must be mapped into both ecosystems consistently. We define an error translation table with categories (USER_ERROR, TOOL_FAILURE, TIMEOUT, INTERNAL) and recommend mapping strategies for older SDKs. - Rollback and fallback: If the shim detects repeated mismatches (schema failure rates above threshold), it should automatically fall back to the original legacy routing and emit an alert to the route owner.
